title: The detached bundle SIGNATURE file (ACP-SPEC-001 §8.2, PB-8)
description:
The `SIGNATURE` file at the bundle root: the declared suite, and one signature value per primitive that suite requires, over SHA-256 of the canonical bundle tree.

A CORRECTION IS RECORDED HERE. Until this revision this file was named `bundle.schema.json` and described a *tree index* — `schema_version`, a `members` array of path+digest pairs, and a `signature` object carrying two fixed base64 fields named `classical` and `pq`. None of that artifact exists. §8.2's file listing contains no index file; the covered set is established by the CANONICAL WALK (`walk_bundle`, in both implementations), which is what makes "the tree" a fact rather than a convention. And PB-8, added in v1.3.15 when the offline signer turned the format from a diagram into bytes, specifies the file as a suite plus ONE VALUE PER PRIMITIVE — a map keyed by primitive name, hex-encoded — which is not the fixed pair the old schema declared.

So the normative source held two descriptions of one object, and they disagreed: the encoding-split defect arriving inside the document that exists to prevent it. It survived because NOTHING READ THE SCHEMAS. They were normative and unexecuted, and the first consumer — `tools/codegen.sh` — found this on its first run. That is the same shape as `sim/bundle.py` silently dropping three fields from a hash for several releases: a load-bearing artifact with no gate line.

WHY THE MEMBERS INDEX IS NOT COMING BACK. The old rationale was real — without an explicit list, a verifier that skipped a file and a signer that included it compute different hashes and neither can tell which is wrong. The adopted answer is to make the WALK normative rather than to ship a list: it refuses symlinks, refuses unrecognised file types, and orders byte-wise, so two conformant implementations enumerate the same set. A committed index would be a second statement of the same fact, and this file exists because of what happens to the second statement.

suite.description: The suite this signature was produced under. PB-8: it MUST be inside the tree hash. Outside it, an attacker relabels a hybrid bundle as classical, the verifier obligingly requires one primitive, and the CR-3 downgrade costs nothing.

parts.description:
primitive name -> signature value, lowercase hex.

CR-3, CONJUNCTIVE: the values present MUST be exactly those the declared suite requires, and every one of them MUST verify. Not "at least": a value for a primitive the suite does not declare is as much a refusal as a missing one, because an `any`-shaped check lets an attacker strip the post-quantum leg, present a genuine classical signature, and be accepted.

Hex rather than base64, matching what both implementations write. Per-primitive lengths (Ed25519 64 bytes, ML-DSA-65 3309) are asserted in code and not here: `parts` is keyed by primitive, so no single value pattern can express a length that depends on its own key.

x-acp-absent.why: a primitive the declared suite requires and this file does not carry is a stripped leg, and a stripped leg is the downgrade the hybrid suite exists to prevent. Absent is refused, never treated as 'not applicable'.

suite_id.description:
A suite NAME as it appears on the wire.

DELIBERATELY NOT ORDERED. There is no `x-acp-ordered` here and there must not be one: CR-4's floor is satisfied by CONTAINMENT of primitives, not by rank. A generated `Ord` would make `declared >= floor` compile, and that comparison is the downgrade — `ed25519` and `slhdsa128s` are incomparable, not adjacent. The behavioural type is `acp_crypto::Suite`, which carries `satisfies_floor` and `primitives()`; this is the wire name and nothing more.

NOT `const`. Listing only the hybrid suite would make a bundle signed under `ed25519` fail SHAPE validation, when the required outcome is a CR-4 refusal naming the floor. Unknown names outside this list are refused under CR-1 by the loader, never defaulted to a known suite.

primitive.description:
A primitive NAME as it appears on the wire.

`pq-slh` is declared and NOT implemented. It keeps its own name and fails closed — aliasing it to `pq` would let a verifier report success for a primitive it cannot compute, which is the one thing an unimplemented primitive must never do.
